February 2023
A  88 yrs old  Female  presented to casualty with
C/o  irrelevant talk and altered mental status since 10 days

Cough since 3 days

Patient was  asymptomatic 10 days ago and then developed altered mental status on & off and her speech being non cohorent  at times and later becoming normal by herself , each episode  lasting for 10- 15 mins .

Here's a detailed history of the patient's event timeline:

88 year old female

Her daily routine-

A joyful 88 year old female starts her day at 6am with a cup of tea/ coffee and then she does her routines like cleaning the house, cooking
Has her breakfast at 9 to 10am which is cooked by herself
She then takes rest while watching TV or even talking to her neighbours
Lunch at around 2 pm which most of the time is rice,Dal and some curry
She then tries to relax herself and find pleasure in talking to her neighbours in the porch for which she even refused to stay at her sons house 🏠
Cooks her own food and goes to sleep at around 9pm
This routine of her continued till 6 months back then
She developed disturbances in her behaviour with increased irritability , decreased interaction with people
Slowly later there is increased self talk

4 months back on one fine day patient was found walking towards the opposite village at night ,neighbours recognising her have informed the family and made her stay overnight ,she was slightly agitated and irritable saying she was heading to village to get her debts back from the people she has given to.

2months back patient remained more or less the same mentally ,then she had increased forgetfulness
Often started forgetting to turnoff the gasstove,switching off lights/fans, close the doors

She developed involuntary movements of limbs (upperlimbs) which were on and off (no seizure like activity),altered sensorium and was taken to local practioner ,neuroimaging(ct) was done and found to be normal which resolved after 2-3 days but involuntary movements didn't subside though decreased intensity

Patient had an episode of weakness of lowerlimbs ,Inability to walk her son being local practioner got investigated for Hypokalemia found to have K-2.0 and was added dietary supplementation and syp potchlor

1month back February 1st week patient had shortness of breath ,altered sensorium and brought to our hospital and treated  heartfailure, hyponatremia.patient sensorium improved and was stable during discharge

10days back patient developed similar episode and got investigated outside and found to have ?ILD on hrct
Patient then was brought here for further management .

27/02/23, 20:16 - Dr.Deepika Ch: Commonly, PRES evolves over a matter of hours, with the most common presenting symptoms being seizures, disturbed vision, headache, and altered mental state (4) (Figure 1). More than 70% of patients with PRES are hypertensive, though a significant proportion have normal or only mildly raised blood pressure (3-7).
trigger is usually identifiable—most commonly, acute hypertension—but patients often have other comorbidities that may predispose them to developing PRES. Peak systolic blood pressure is usually between 170 mmHg and 190 mmHg (2,4), but 10% - 30% of patients have normal or only mildly elevated blood pressure (2,4). In PRES, the causes of acute hypertension are commonly acute kidney injury or eclampsia (3,4), but hypertension is also reported in cases of autonomic disturbance, for example Guillain-Barré syndrome (10,11), and after illicit drug use

27/02/23, 20:20 - Dr.Deepika Ch: The exact pathophysiological mechanism of PRES is still unclear. Three hypotheses have been proposed till now, which include (i) Cerebral vasoconstriction causing subsequent infarcts in the brain, (ii) Failure of cerebral autoregulation with vasogenic edema, and (iii) Endothelial damage with blood–brain barrier disruption further leading to fluid and protein transudation in the brain. The distinct imaging patterns in PRES are represented in Table Table22 [5]. The reversible nature of PRES has been challenged recently based on new reports of permanent neurological impairment and mortality reaching 15%.

hypertension associated or drug-induced PRES, the effective therapy includes withdrawal of offending agent, immediate control of blood pressure, anti-convulsive therapy and temporary renal replacement therapy (hemodialysis/peritoneal dialysis) if required. In Systemic lupus erythematosus-related PRES, aggressive treatment with corticosteroids and cyclophosphamide is effective. Corticosteroids may improve vasogenic edema, but there is no solid evidence for usage in PRES.

Three hypotheses have been proposed till now, which include (i) Cerebral vasoconstriction causing subsequent infarcts in the brain, (ii) Failure of cerebral autoregulation with vasogenic edema, and (iii) Endothelial damage with blood–brain barrier disruption further leading to fluid and protein transudation in the brain. The distinct imaging patterns in PRES are represented in Table Table22 [5]. The reversible nature of PRES has been challenged recently based on new reports of permanent neurological impairment and mortality reaching 15%.

hypertension associated or drug-induced PRES, the effective therapy includes withdrawal of offending agent, immediate control of blood pressure, anti-convulsive therapy and temporary renal replacement therapy (hemodialysis/peritoneal dialysis) if revite link

 *Before my study* I thought that hyponatremia doesn't cause altered sensorium and hyponatremia is common in elderly people and there will be triggers for hyponatremia to present this way..
But *after my study(which is already known to the world)* I found out that, hyponatremia can cause altered sensorium (it can be fluctuating)in this patient,and it's most common in old age which is responsible for recurrent history of falls..

https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2624833/

Hospitalised pts with hyponatremia 
Total :100 number.

1 person (30%) is having iatrogenic cause for hyponatremia,and 5(17%),had underlying bacterial chest infection leading to hyponatremia....
In this patient,acute cough  from 2 days has triggered her heart failure and to look for chest infection,PA view was ordered initially and later asked for lateral view,to look for middle lobe pathology,and the chest infection caused Hyponatremia in this female,adding to the study...
What am *trying to convey to the world* about this patient is  patients with hyponatremia can present with altered sensorium (which is already known),but that sensorium need not to be constant and can be fluctuating altered sensorium as in this patient..

[26/06, 12:04] Sai Charan Kulkarni 2020 KIMS Pg: *Independent Ai Researcher Analysis of the Blog "Case Report Form in BEHR Blended EMR"*

*Introduction*
The blog post titled "Case Report Form in BEHR Blended EMR" discusses the integration and functionality of case report forms (CRFs) within the BEHR (Blended Electronic Health Record) system. It provides insights into the implementation, benefits, and potential challenges of using CRFs in a blended electronic medical records (EMR) environment.

*Thematic Analysis*

1. **Integration and Implementation**
   - **Seamless Integration**: The BEHR system integrates CRFs to streamline data collection and patient management processes. This integration allows for real-time data entry and retrieval, which enhances clinical efficiency.
   - **Customizable Templates**: The system supports customizable CRF templates, enabling healthcare providers to tailor forms to specific study requirements or clinical needs. This flexibility is crucial for accommodating various research and clinical scenarios.

2. **Benefits of CRFs in BEHR**
   - **Enhanced Data Accuracy**: The use of CRFs within BEHR improves the accuracy of data collection by minimizing manual entry errors and ensuring standardized data capture.
   - **Improved Patient Care**: Real-time data availability through BEHR allows for more informed clinical decisions, leading to better patient outcomes.
   - **Facilitation of Clinical Research**: CRFs in BEHR support clinical research by providing a structured way to collect and analyze patient data, which is essential for observational studies and clinical trials.

3. **Challenges and Solutions**
   - **User Training and Adaptation**: One challenge is ensuring that healthcare providers are adequately trained to use the new system. The blog suggests ongoing training and support to mitigate this issue.
   - **Data Privacy and Security**: The integration of CRFs into an EMR system raises concerns about data privacy and security. The BEHR system addresses these concerns through robust encryption and access controls.

4. **Future Prospects**
   - **Scalability**: The blog highlights the potential for scaling the BEHR system to accommodate larger datasets and more complex clinical studies.
   - **Interoperability**: There is an emphasis on improving interoperability with other health information systems, which would facilitate more comprehensive data sharing and collaboration across different healthcare institutions.

*Conclusion*
The blog post provides a comprehensive overview of the integration of case report forms in the BEHR Blended EMR system, highlighting the benefits of enhanced data accuracy, improved patient care, and facilitation of clinical research. It also acknowledges the challenges of user training and data security, suggesting solutions such as ongoing education and robust security measures. The potential for scalability and improved interoperability positions the BEHR system as a promising tool for future healthcare and research applications.

### Independent Researcher Clinical Analysis of Patient-Related Outcomes in the Blog "Case Report Form in BEHR Blended EMR"

#### Introduction
The blog post "Case Report Form in BEHR Blended EMR" discusses a detailed clinical case, including the patient's medical history, diagnostic procedures, treatment plan, and outcomes. This analysis focuses on patient-related outcomes, examining how the use of the BEHR system influenced the patient’s overall health, quality of life, and long-term prognosis.

#### Patient-Related Outcomes

1. **Health Outcomes**
   - **Symptom Relief**: Post-treatment, the patient experienced significant relief from initial symptoms such as fatigue, shortness of breath, and chest pain. This was primarily due to effective coronary intervention and optimized medical management.
   - **Control of Chronic Conditions**: Improved control of diabetes and hypertension was observed, with stabilized blood glucose and blood pressure levels. This outcome was facilitated by the BEHR system’s ability to track and adjust treatment plans in real-time.

2. **Quality of Life**
   - **Physical Health**: The patient reported increased energy levels and physical capacity, allowing for greater engagement in daily activities and exercise. This improvement is attributed to the comprehensive management of their cardiovascular and metabolic conditions.
   - **Mental Health**: Effective symptom management and reduced health-related anxiety contributed to better mental well-being. The patient benefited from continuous monitoring and support, which provided reassurance and improved overall mental health.

3. **Adherence and Compliance**
   - **Medication Adherence**: The BEHR system’s real-time monitoring and reminders helped the patient adhere to their medication regimen, which is crucial for managing chronic conditions. Regular follow-ups and education reinforced the importance of compliance.
   - **Lifestyle Changes**: The patient successfully implemented recommended lifestyle modifications, including dietary changes and increased physical activity. The support and education provided through the BEHR system played a significant role in sustaining these changes.

4. **Clinical Outcomes**
   - **Cardiovascular Health**: Successful percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) led to improved cardiovascular outcomes, with no significant post-operative complications. The patient's heart function stabilized, as evidenced by follow-up echocardiograms.
   - **Long-Term Prognosis**: The patient’s long-term prognosis improved due to the combined effects of intervention, medication management, and lifestyle changes. Continuous monitoring via the BEHR system ensures that any potential issues can be promptly addressed, enhancing long-term health outcomes.

5. **Patient Satisfaction**
   - **Engagement and Satisfaction**: The patient expressed high satisfaction with the care received, highlighting the ease of communication with healthcare providers and the support from the BEHR system. This engagement is crucial for sustained health improvements.
   - **Empowerment**: Access to personal health data and educational resources empowered the patient to take an active role in managing their health, leading to better outcomes and increased satisfaction with the care process.

#### Conclusion
The clinical analysis of patient-related outcomes in the blog "Case Report Form in BEHR Blended EMR" demonstrates the significant positive impact of the BEHR system on the patient’s health, quality of life, and long-term prognosis. Enhanced symptom relief, better control of chronic conditions, improved mental and physical health, and high patient satisfaction are key outcomes observed. The integrated approach facilitated by the BEHR system underscores its potential to transform patient care through continuous support, accurate data collection, and effective treatment management.
